DEBUGLEVEL=1

function repeat_char() {
  local char=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  local count=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  local result=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  if [[ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$char&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; || -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$count&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Usage: repeat_char &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;character&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;count&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;2
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$count&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; -lt 0 ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Count must be a non-negative integer.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;2
    return 1
  fi

  for ((i = 0; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; count; i++)); do
    result+=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$char&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  done

  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$result&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}
function longest_string_length() {
  local max_length=0
  local current_length
  local line

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    current_length=${#line}
    if [[ $current_length -gt $max_length ]]; then
      max_length=$current_length
    fi
  done

  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$max_length&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}
function fecho() {
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$FUNCNAME : $1 $2 $3 $4 $5&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}
function fdebug() {
    if [ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$DEBUGLEVEL&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; -gt &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;0&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
        echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;DBG $FUNCNAME : $1 $2 $3 $4 $&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    fi
}
# show up to 3 parent dirs, except ~, resolve all other dir aliases
function git_toplevel() {
     if [ -d &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;.git&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
         git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null | sed -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;s,^$HOME,~,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
     fi
}
function git_branch() {
     #git branch 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null | sed -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;/^[^*]/d&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/* \(.*\)/ (\1)/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
     if [ -d &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;.git&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
         git branch 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null | sed &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/^..//&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; | sed &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/master/m/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
     fi
}
function git_origin() {
     # git branch 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null | sed -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;/^[^*]/d&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/* \(.*\)/ (\1)/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
     if [ -d &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;.git&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
         git config --get remote.origin.url 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null
     fi
}
function git_originsync() {
     if [ -d &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;.git&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
         git config color.ui false
         git branch -vv 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null |  gawk &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;match($0, /\[([^\]]+)\]/, a) { print a[1] }&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; | sed &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/origin/o/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; | sed &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/master/m/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; | sed &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/ ahead /+/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
     else
         echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
     fi
}
function collapse_pwd() {
    curr_pwd=$(pwd | sed -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;s,^$HOME,~,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
    echo $curr_pwd
}
function collapse_hostname() {
    curr_hostname=$(hostname)
    echo $curr_hostname
}

function backup_file() {
  local filename=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  local backup_dir=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # New argument for backup directory
  local timestamp=$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
  local backup_filename=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${filename##*/}.backup.${timestamp}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Extract filename only
  local backup_path=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${backup_dir}/${backup_filename}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  if [ -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
    if [ -d &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$backup_dir&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then # Check if backup directory exists
      cp &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$backup_path&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
      #echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;File &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; backed up to &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$backup_path&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    else
      #echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: Backup directory &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$backup_dir&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; does not exist.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
      return 1
    fi

  else
    #echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: File &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; not found.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi
}
# Example usage:
# backup_file my_file.txt /path/to/backup/directory


# ****************************************************************************************************
# ****************************************************************************************************

# --- String Manipulation ---

# Trims leading and trailing whitespace from a string.
function trim() {
  local str=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  printf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%s&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${str#&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${str%%[![:space:]]*}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${str%&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${str##*[![:space:]]}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}
remove_leading_whitespace() {
         local input=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       # Bash-Function-Args
  local output=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${input#&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${input%%[![:space:]]*}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$output&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Checks if a string starts with a given prefix.
function starts_with() {
         local string=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local prefix=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  # Bash-Function-Args
  [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$string&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; == &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$prefix&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;* ]]
}

# Checks if a string ends with a given suffix.
function ends_with() {
         local string=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local suffix=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  # Bash-Function-Args
  [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$string&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; == *&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$suffix&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]
}

# Checks if a string contains a substring.
function contains() {
         local string=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local substring=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  # Bash-Function-Args
  [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$string&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; == *&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$substring&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;* ]]
}

# Replaces all occurrences of a substring in a string.
function replace() {
         local string=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local old=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local new=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$3&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  # Bash-Function-Args
  printf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%s\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${string//$old/$new}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Extracts a substring based on start and end indices. (1-based indexing)
function substring() {
         local string=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local start=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local length=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$3&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  # Bash-Function-Args
  if [[ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$length&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    printf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%s\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${string:$((start - 1))}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  else
    printf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%s\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${string:$((start - 1)):$length}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  fi
}

# --- File and Directory Operations ---

# Creates a directory if it doesn&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t exist.
function mkdir_p() {
  mkdir -p &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Checks if a file or directory exists.
function exists() {
  [[ -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]
}

# Checks if a file exists.
function is_file() {
  [[ -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]
}

# Checks if a directory exists.
function is_dir() {
  [[ -d &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]
}

# Gets the absolute path of a file or directory.
function abspath() {
  local path=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  if [[ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$path&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    pwd
  else
    realpath &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$path&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  fi
}

# Gets the filename from a path.
function basename() {
  local path=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  printf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%s\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$(basename &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$path&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Gets the directory from a path.
function dirname() {
  local path=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  printf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%s\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$(dirname &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$path&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Gets the file extension from a path.
function extension() {
  local path=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  printf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%s\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${path##*.}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Copies a file or directory recursively.
function cp_r() {
  cp -r &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Moves a file or directory.
function mv_f() {
  mv -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Removes a file or directory recursively.
function rm_rf() {
  rm -rf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# --- System and Process Utilities ---

# Checks if a command is available.
function command_exists() {
  command -v &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null
}

# Gets the process ID (PID) of a process by name.
function pidof_name() {
         local name=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               # Bash-Function-Args
  pidof &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$name&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Kills a process by name.
function kill_name() {
         local name=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               # Bash-Function-Args
  pkill &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$name&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Kills a process by PID.
function kill_pid() {
         local pid=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               # Bash-Function-Args
  kill &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$pid&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# Runs a command and returns its exit code.
function run_and_exit_code() {
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$@&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  echo $?
}

# Runs a command and returns its output.
function run_and_output() {
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$@&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

#Runs a command and returns its error.
function run_and_error() {
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$@&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1 &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null
}
# --- Array Manipulation ---

# Checks if an array contains a value.
function array_contains() {
         local needle=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               # Bash-Function-Args
  shift
  local haystack=(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${@}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
  local found=0
  for item in &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${haystack[@]}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;; do
    if [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$item&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; == &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$needle&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
      found=1
      break
    fi
  done
  if [[ $found -eq 1 ]]; then
    return 0 # True
  else
    return 1 # False
  fi
}

# Joins array elements with a delimiter.
function array_join() {
         local delimiter=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               # Bash-Function-Args
  shift
  local array=(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${@}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
  local IFS=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$delimiter&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${array[*]}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# --- Networking ---

# Checks if a host is reachable.
function is_reachable() {
  ping -c 1 -W 1 &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null
}

# Checks if a port is open.
# is_port_open() {
#   timeout 1 bash -c &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;/dev/tcp/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
# }

# --- Input/Output ---

# Prints a message to stderr.
function eprint() {
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;2
}

# Reads a line from stdin with a prompt.
function read_prompt() {
  read -p &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}

# --- Time and Date ---

# Gets the current timestamp in milliseconds.
function timestamp_ms() {
  date +%s%3N
}

function scan_for_secrets() {
         local file=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               # Bash-Function-Args

  if [[ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Usage: scan_for_secrets &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ ! -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: File &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; not found.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  # Define patterns to search for (add/modify as needed)
  local patterns=(
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;API_KEY=[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;SECRET_KEY=[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;PASSWORD=[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{8,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=[A-Z0-9]{20}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;ssh-rsa [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;ssh-ed25519 [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Bearer [A-Za-z0-9._-]{20,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Authorization: Basic [A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Authorization: Token [A-Za-z0-9]{20,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; #look for username:password type strings.
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;PGPASSWORD=[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{8,}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # postgres password
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;DATABASE_URL=postgres://[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+@&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # postgres database url, catches username and password.
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;MONGO_URI=mongodb://[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+@&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; #mongodb uri, catches username and password
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;password[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  # Basic password pattern
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;secret[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;   # Secret pattern
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;key[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      # Key pattern
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[A-Z0-9]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # AWS Access Key ID
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[a-zA-Z0-9/+=]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # AWS Secret Access Key
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;api_key[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # API Key pattern
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;database_url[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Database URL
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;connection_string[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Connection String
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;private_key[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Private Key
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;client_secret[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Client Secret
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;oauth_token[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # OAuth Token
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;bearer_token[[:space:]]*[:=][[:space:]]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[^\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]*[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Bearer Token
  )

    # &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;export [A-Z_]+=[\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]?[A-Za-z0-9_\\-./+=@$%^&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;*()!~`?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;:;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;]+&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # look for exported environment variables.
  local found=0

  for pattern in &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${patterns[@]}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;; do
    if grep -E &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$pattern&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; /dev/null; then
      found=1
      echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Potential secret found in &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; matching pattern: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$pattern&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
      grep -E &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$pattern&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    fi
  done

  if [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$found&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;No potential secrets found in &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  fi

  return 0
}

function isSameHash() {
    local FILE=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               # Bash-Function-Args
    local tmp=/tmp/HASHCHECK_$$
    local CH=$(md5sum &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$FILE&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; | awk &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;{print $1}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;)
    if [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$CH&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; == &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$OH&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
        echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    else
        echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;0&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    fi
}

function padout_file_lines() {
         local filename=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;    # Bash-Function-Args
  local tmp1=$(mktemp)
  local tmp2=$(mktemp)
  rm -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1
  rm -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1

  if [[ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    fecho &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: Filename not provided.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ ! -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    fecho &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: File &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; not found.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  sed &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/[[:space:]]*$//&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  max_len=$(wc -L &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; | awk &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;{print $1}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;)
  padding_length=$((max_len + 0))

  # Iterate through each line of the file and pad it
  rm -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    printf &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%-${padding_length}s\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$line&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Pad to the right
  done &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  mv &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  rm -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1
  rm -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1
  return 0
}

# Function to split a file into N files
function split_file_n() {
         local input_file=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local num_files=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Bash-Function-Args
  local prefix=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${3:-split_}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Default prefix is &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;split_&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  if [[ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; || -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$num_files&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Usage: split_file_n &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;number_of_files&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; [prefix]&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ ! -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: Input file &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; not found.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  if ! [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$num_files&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
      echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: Number of files must be a positive integer.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
      return 1
  fi

  local total_lines=$(wc -l &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
  local lines_per_file=$((total_lines / num_files))
  local remainder=$((total_lines % num_files))

  local start_line=1
  for ((i=1; i&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;=num_files; i++)); do
    local output_file=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${prefix}${i}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    local current_lines=$lines_per_file

    if [[ $i -le $remainder ]]; then
      ((current_lines++)) # Distribute remainder lines
    fi

    head -n &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$((start_line + current_lines - 1))&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; | tail -n &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$current_lines&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$output_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    ((start_line += current_lines))
  done
}

function truncate_file_lines() {
         local filename=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local num_chars=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Bash-Function-Args

  if [[ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Truncate Error: Filename not provided.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ ! -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Truncate Error: File &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; not found.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$num_chars&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Truncate Error: Number of characters not provided.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  if ! [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$num_chars&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Truncate Error: Number of characters must be a positive integer.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$num_chars&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; == &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;0&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    return 0
  fi

  local temp_file=$(mktemp)

  while IFS= read -r line; do

function justify_line() {
         local str=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;; local num=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; # Bash-Function-Args

    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; | gawk -v num=$2 &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
        function justify(szIn,  l,n,i,sz,m,k,A, flag) {
            sz = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
            n =  split(szIn,A,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
            r = 1
            delim = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
            flag=0
            for (i=1; i&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;=n; i++) {
                sz = delim sz A[i] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
                delim = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
                l = l + length(A[i] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
                if (l &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; (num*r)) {
                    r=r+1;
                    sz = sz &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
                    flag=1
                    delim = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
                }
            }
            if (flag == 1) sz = sz &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
            return sz;
        }
        {
            print justify($0);
        }&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    cat &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    rm -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1
}

function create_markdown_table4() {
         local input_file=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;local str=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;                   # Bash-Function-Args
  local tmp=$(mktemp)
  local LEN=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  local STRING=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  # Check if the input file exists
  if [[ ! -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    fecho &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: Input file &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; not found.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  LEN=`longest_string_length &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;`
  STRING=`repeat_char &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;-&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;24&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;`

  rm -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1
  if [[ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$str&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; == &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;MAKELINKS&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
      cat &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; |sort|uniq|gawk &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;{n=split($0,A,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;/&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;[&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; A[n] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;](&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; $0 &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; $tmp
  else
      cat &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; |sort|uniq &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; $tmp
  fi

  # Read lines from the file and create table rows
  local line_count=0
  local row=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  local first_row=1

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    if [[ $line_count -eq 0 ]]; then
      if [[ $first_row -eq 1 ]]; then
          echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;| $STRING | $STRING | $STRING | $STRING |&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
          echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;|----------|----------|----------|----------|&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
          first_row=0
      fi
    fi

    row+=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;| $line &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    line_count=$((line_count + 1))

    if [[ $line_count -eq 4 ]]; then
      echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$row|&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
      row=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
      line_count=0
    fi
  done &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$tmp&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  # Handle remaining lines if the total line count is not a multiple of 5
  if [[ $line_count -gt 0 ]]; then
    for ((i = line_count; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; 5; i++)); do
        row+=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;|  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    done
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$row|&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  fi
}

# Trims leading and trailing whitespace from a string.
function trim(str,  trimmed) {
  sub(/^[ \t\r\n]+/, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, str);
  sub(/[ \t\r\n]+$/, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, str);
  return str;
}

# Splits a string into an array based on a delimiter, handles empty fields
function split_preserve_empty(str, arr, delim,  i, field) {
  delete arr;
  i = 1;
  while (match(str, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;([^&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; delim &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;]*)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; delim &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;?&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, field)) {
    arr[i++] = field[1];
    str = substr(str, RLENGTH + 1);
  }
  if (length(str) &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; 0) {
    arr[i] = str;
  }
  return i;
}

# Checks if a string starts with a given prefix.
function starts_with(str, prefix) {
  return substr(str, 1, length(prefix)) == prefix;
}

# Checks if a string ends with a given suffix.
function ends_with(str, suffix) {
  return substr(str, length(str) - length(suffix) + 1) == suffix;
}

# Replaces all occurrences of a substring with another string.
function replace_all(str, from, to,  result) {
  result = str;
  while (sub(from, to, result)) {}
  return result;
}

#Checks if a string contains a given substring
function contains(str, sub) {
    return index(str, sub) != 0;
}

# --- Array Manipulation ---

# Checks if an array contains a given value.
function array_contains(arr, val,  i) {
  for (i in arr) {
    if (arr[i] == val) {
      return 1;
    }
  }
  return 0;
}

# Joins array elements into a string with a delimiter.
function array_join(arr, delim,  i, result) {
  result = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
  for (i in arr) {
    result = result (result == &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ? &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; : delim) arr[i];
  }
  return result;
}

#Filters an array based on a given condition (function).
function array_filter(arr, filter_func,  i, new_arr, index) {
    delete new_arr;
    index = 1;
    for (i in arr){
        if(filter_func(arr[i])){
            new_arr[index++] = arr[i];
        }
    }
    return index -1; #Return the size of the new array.
}

#Maps an array to a new array using a function.
function array_map(arr, map_func,  i, new_arr, index){
    delete new_arr;
    index = 1;
    for(i in arr){
        new_arr[index++] = map_func(arr[i]);
    }
    return index -1;
}

# --- Data Processing ---

# Calculates the sum of values in an array.
function array_sum(arr,  i, sum) {
  sum = 0;
  for (i in arr) {
    sum += arr[i];
  }
  return sum;
}

# Calculates the average of values in an array.
function array_average(arr,  sum, count) {
  sum = array_sum(arr);
  count = length(arr);
  if (count == 0) {
    return 0;
  }
  return sum / count;
}

#Parses CSV data into a 2D array.
function parse_csv(data, arr, delimiter,  lines, i, fields, j) {
    lines = split(data, lines, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;\n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
    for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= lines; i++) {
        split_preserve_empty(lines[i], fields, delimiter);
        for (j = 1; j &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= length(fields); j++) {
            arr[i, j] = fields[j];
        }
    }
    return lines;
}

# --- List Operations (Arrays as Lists) ---

# Append an element to the end of a list (array).
function list_append(arr, val,  len) {
  len = length(arr) + 1;
  arr[len] = val;
  return len;
}

# Prepend an element to the beginning of a list (array).
function list_prepend(arr, val,  i, temp_arr, len) {
    len = length(arr);
    for(i = len; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;= 1; i--){
        temp_arr[i+1] = arr[i];
    }
    arr[1] = val;
    for(i = 2; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len+1; i++){
        arr[i] = temp_arr[i];
    }
    return len +1;
}

# Insert an element at a specific index in a list (array).
function list_insert(arr, index, val,  i, temp_arr, len) {
  len = length(arr);
  if (index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; 1 || index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; len + 1) {
    return len; # Invalid index, return original length.
  }

  for (i = len; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;= index; i--) {
    temp_arr[i + 1] = arr[i];
  }
  arr[index] = val;
  for (i = index + 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len + 1; i++) {
    arr[i] = temp_arr[i];
  }
  return len + 1;
}

# Remove an element at a specific index in a list (array).
function list_remove_at(arr, index,  i, len) {
  len = length(arr);
  if (index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; 1 || index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; len) {
    return len; # Invalid index, return original length.
  }

  for (i = index; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; len; i++) {
    arr[i] = arr[i + 1];
  }
  delete arr[len];
  return len - 1;
}

# Remove the first occurrence of a value from a list (array).
function list_remove_value(arr, val,  i, len) {
  len = length(arr);
  for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len; i++) {
    if (arr[i] == val) {
      list_remove_at(arr, i);
      return len - 1;
    }
  }
  return len; # Value not found, return original length.
}

# Get the element at a specific index in a list (array).
function list_get(arr, index,  len) {
  len = length(arr);
  if (index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; 1 || index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; len) {
    return &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;; # Invalid index, return empty string.
  }
  return arr[index];
}

# Get the index of the first occurrence of a value in a list (array).
function list_index_of(arr, val,  i, len) {
  len = length(arr);
  for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len; i++) {
    if (arr[i] == val) {
      return i;
    }
  }
  return -1; # Value not found, return -1.
}

# Get the last index of a value in a list (array).
function list_last_index_of(arr, val, i, len, last_index){
    len = length(arr);
    last_index = -1;
    for(i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len; i++){
        if(arr[i] == val){
            last_index = i;
        }
    }
    return last_index;
}

# Reverse a list (array).
function list_reverse(arr,  i, len, temp_arr) {
  len = length(arr);
  for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len; i++) {
    temp_arr[i] = arr[i];
  }
  for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len; i++) {
    arr[i] = temp_arr[len - i + 1];
  }
  return len;
}

# Slice a list (array) from start_index to end_index (inclusive).
function list_slice(arr, start_index, end_index,  i, len, new_arr, new_index) {
  len = length(arr);
  if (start_index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; 1) {
    start_index = 1;
  }
  if (end_index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; len) {
    end_index = len;
  }
  if (start_index &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; end_index) {
    return 0; # Empty slice, return 0.
  }

  delete new_arr;
  new_index = 1;
  for (i = start_index; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= end_index; i++) {
    new_arr[new_index++] = arr[i];
  }
  return new_index - 1;
}

# Concatenate two lists (arrays).
function list_concat(arr1, arr2,  i, len1, len2, new_arr, new_index) {
  len1 = length(arr1);
  len2 = length(arr2);
  delete new_arr;
  new_index = 1;
  for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len1; i++) {
    new_arr[new_index++] = arr1[i];
  }
  for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= len2; i++) {
    new_arr[new_index++] = arr2[i];
  }
  return new_index - 1;
}

# --- Example Usage (Illustrative) ---
BEGIN {
  # String manipulation examples
  str = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;   hello world   &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;[&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; trim(str) &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;]&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;

  text = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;apple,banana,,orange&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
  count = split_preserve_empty(text, fruits, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
  for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= count; i++) {
    print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Fruit &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;: [&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; fruits[i] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;]&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
  }

  print starts_with(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;awk is fun&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;awk&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
  print ends_with(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;awk is fun&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;fun&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
  print replace_all(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;awk is fun&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;fun&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;powerful&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
  print contains(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;awk is fun&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;is&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);

  # Array manipulation examples
  numbers[1] = 10; numbers[2] = 20; numbers[3] = 30;
  print array_contains(numbers, 20);
  print array_join(numbers, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
  print array_sum(numbers);
  print array_average(numbers);

  # CSV parsing example
  csv_data = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;name,age,city\nJohn,30,New York\nJane,25,London&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
  rows = parse_csv(csv_data, csv_array, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
  for (i = 1; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;= rows; i++) {
    print csv_array[i, 1] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; csv_array[i, 2] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; csv_array[i, 3];
  }

  # Array filter and map examples
  function is_even(num){return num % 2 == 0;}
  even_count = array_filter(numbers, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;is_even&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, even_numbers);
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Even numbers: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; array_join(even_numbers, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);

  function double(num){return num * 2;}
  doubled_count = array_map(numbers, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;double&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, doubled_numbers);
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Doubled numbers: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; array_join(doubled_numbers, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);

  # List operation examples
  list[1] = 10; list[2] = 20; list[3] = 30;

  list_append(list, 40);
  list_prepend(list, 5);
  list_insert(list, 3, 25);
  list_remove_at(list, 4);
  list_remove_value(list, 20);

  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;List: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; array_join(list, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Get index 2: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; list_get(list, 2);
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Index of 30: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; list_index_of(list, 30);
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Last Index of 10: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; list_last_index_of(list,10);
  list_reverse(list);
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Reversed list: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; array_join(list, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);

  list2[1] = 100; list2[2] = 200;
  list_concat(list, list2, combined_list);
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Combined List: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; array_join(combined_list, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);

  list_slice(combined_list, 2, 4, sliced_list);
  print &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Sliced List: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; array_join(sliced_list, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;);
}

Global

:h[elp] keyword - open help for keyword
:sav[eas] file - save file as
:clo[se] - close current pane
:ter[minal] - open a terminal window
K - open man page for word under the cursor
Tip Run vimtutor in a terminal to learn the first Vim commands.

Cursor movement

h - move cursor left
j - move cursor down
k - move cursor up
l - move cursor right
gj - move cursor down (multi-line text)
gk - move cursor up (multi-line text)
H - move to top of screen
M - move to middle of screen
L - move to bottom of screen
w - jump forwards to the start of a word
W - jump forwards to the start of a word (words can contain punctuation)
e - jump forwards to the end of a word
E - jump forwards to the end of a word (words can contain punctuation)
b - jump backwards to the start of a word
B - jump backwards to the start of a word (words can contain punctuation)
ge - jump backwards to the end of a word
gE - jump backwards to the end of a word (words can contain punctuation)
% - move cursor to matching character (default supported pairs: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;{}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;[]&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; 
- use :h matchpairs in vim for more info)
0 - jump to the start of the line
^ - jump to the first non-blank character of the line
$ - jump to the end of the line
g_ - jump to the last non-blank character of the line
gg - go to the first line of the document
G - go to the last line of the document
5gg or 5G - go to line 5
gd - move to local declaration
gD - move to global declaration
fx - jump to next occurrence of character x
tx - jump to before next occurrence of character x
Fx - jump to the previous occurrence of character x
Tx - jump to after previous occurrence of character x
; - repeat previous f, t, F or T movement
, - repeat previous f, t, F or T movement, backwards
} - jump to next paragraph (or function/block, when editing code)
{ - jump to previous paragraph (or function/block, when editing code)
zz - center cursor on screen
zt - position cursor on top of the screen
zb - position cursor on bottom of the screen
Ctrl + e - move screen down one line (without moving cursor)
Ctrl + y - move screen up one line (without moving cursor)
Ctrl + b - move screen up one page (cursor to last line)
Ctrl + f - move screen down one page (cursor to first line)
Ctrl + d - move cursor and screen down 1/2 page
Ctrl + u - move cursor and screen up 1/2 page

Insert mode - inserting/appending text

i - insert before the cursor
I - insert at the beginning of the line
a - insert (append) after the cursor
A - insert (append) at the end of the line
o - append (open) a new line below the current line
O - append (open) a new line above the current line
ea - insert (append) at the end of the word
Ctrl + h - delete the character before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + w - delete word before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + j - add a line break at the cursor position during insert mode
Ctrl + t - indent (move right) line one shiftwidth during insert mode
Ctrl + d - de-indent (move left) line one shiftwidth during insert mode
Ctrl + n - insert (auto-complete) next match before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + p - insert (auto-complete) previous match before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + rx - insert the contents of register x
Ctrl + ox - Temporarily enter normal mode to issue one normal-mode command x.
Esc or Ctrl + c - exit insert mode

Editing

r - replace a single character.
R - replace more than one character, until ESC is pressed.
J - join line below to the current one with one space in between
gJ - join line below to the current one without space in between
gwip - reflow paragraph
g~ - switch case up to motion
gu - change to lowercase up to motion
gU - change to uppercase up to motion
cc - change (replace) entire line
c$ or C - change (replace) to the end of the line
ciw - change (replace) entire word
cw or ce - change (replace) to the end of the word
s - delete character and substitute text (same as cl)
S - delete line and substitute text (same as cc)
xp - transpose two letters (delete and paste)
u - undo
U - restore (undo) last changed line
Ctrl + r - redo
. - repeat last command

Marking text (visual mode)

v - start visual mode, mark lines, then do a command (like y-yank)
V - start linewise visual mode
o - move to other end of marked area
Ctrl + v - start visual block mode
O - move to other corner of block
aw - mark a word
ab - a block with ()
aB - a block with {}
at - a block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
ib - inner block with ()
iB - inner block with {}
it - inner block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
Esc or Ctrl + c - exit visual mode

Visual commands

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; - shift text right
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; - shift text left
y - yank (copy) marked text
d - delete marked text
~ - switch case
u - change marked text to lowercase
U - change marked text to uppercase

Registers

:reg[isters] - show registers content
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;xy - yank into register x
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;xp - paste contents of register x
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;+y - yank into the system clipboard register
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;+p - paste from the system clipboard register
Tip Registers are being stored in ~/.viminfo, and will be loaded again on next restart of vim.

Special registers:

0 - last yank
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; - unnamed register, last delete or yank
% - current file name
# - alternate file name
* - clipboard contents (X11 primary)
+ - clipboard contents (X11 clipboard)
/ - last search pattern
: - last command-line
. - last inserted text
- - last small (less than a line) delete
= - expression register
_ - black hole register

Marks and positions

:marks - list of marks
ma - set current position for mark A
`a - jump to position of mark A
y`a - yank text to position of mark A
`0 - go to the position where Vim was previously exited
`&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; - go to the position when last editing this file
`. - go to the position of the last change in this file
`` - go to the position before the last jump
:ju[mps] - list of jumps
Ctrl + i - go to newer position in jump list
Ctrl + o - go to older position in jump list
:changes - list of changes
g, - go to newer position in change list
g; - go to older position in change list
Ctrl + ] - jump to the tag under cursor
Tip To jump to a mark you can either use a backtick (`) or an apostrophe (&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;).
Using an apostrophe jumps to the beginning (first non-blank) of the line holding the mark.

Macros

qa - record macro a
q - stop recording macro
@a - run macro a
@@ - rerun last run macro

Cut and paste

yy - yank (copy) a line
2yy - yank (copy) 2 lines
yw - yank (copy) the characters of the word from the cursor position to the start of the next word
yiw - yank (copy) word under the cursor
yaw - yank (copy) word under the cursor and the space after or before it
y$ or Y - yank (copy) to end of line
p - put (paste) the clipboard after cursor
P - put (paste) before cursor
gp - put (paste) the clipboard after cursor and leave cursor after the new text
gP - put (paste) before cursor and leave cursor after the new text
dd - delete (cut) a line
2dd - delete (cut) 2 lines
dw - delete (cut) the characters of the word from the cursor position to the start of the next word
diw - delete (cut) word under the cursor
daw - delete (cut) word under the cursor and the space after or before it
:3,5d - delete lines starting from 3 to 5
Tip You can also use the following characters to specify the range:
e.g.
:.,$d - From the current line to the end of the file
:.,1d - From the current line to the beginning of the file
:10,1d - From the 10th line to the beginning of the file
:g/{pattern}/d - delete all lines containing pattern
:g!/{pattern}/d - delete all lines not containing pattern
d$ or D - delete (cut) to the end of the line
x - delete (cut) character

Indent text

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; - indent (move right) line one shiftwidth
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; - de-indent (move left) line one shiftwidth
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;% - indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;% - de-indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;ib - indent inner block with ()
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;at - indent a block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
3== - re-indent 3 lines
=% - re-indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
=iB - re-indent inner block with {}
gg=G - re-indent entire buffer
]p - paste and adjust indent to current line

Exiting

:w - write (save) the file, but don&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t exit
:w !sudo tee % - write out the current file using sudo
:wq or :x or ZZ - write (save) and quit
:q - quit (fails if there are unsaved changes)
:q! or ZQ - quit and throw away unsaved changes
:wqa - write (save) and quit on all tabs

Search and replace

/pattern - search for pattern
?pattern - search backward for pattern
\vpattern - &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;very magic&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; pattern: non-alphanumeric characters are interpreted as special regex symbols (no escaping needed)
n - repeat search in same direction
N - repeat search in opposite direction
:%s/old/new/g - replace all old with new throughout file
:%s/old/new/gc - replace all old with new throughout file with confirmations
:noh[lsearch] - remove highlighting of search matches

Search in multiple files

:vim[grep] /pattern/ {`{file}`} - search for pattern in multiple files
e.g. :vim[grep] /foo/ **/*
:cn[ext] - jump to the next match
:cp[revious] - jump to the previous match
:cope[n] - open a window containing the list of matches
:ccl[ose] - close the quickfix window

Tabs

:tabnew or :tabnew {page.words.file} - open a file in a new tab
Ctrl + wT - move the current split window into its own tab
gt or :tabn[ext] - move to the next tab
gT or :tabp[revious] - move to the previous tab
#gt - move to tab number #
:tabm[ove] # - move current tab to the #th position (indexed from 0)
:tabc[lose] - close the current tab and all its windows
:tabo[nly] - close all tabs except for the current one
:tabdo command - run the command on all tabs (e.g. :tabdo q - closes all opened tabs)

Working with multiple files

:e[dit] file - edit a file in a new buffer
:bn[ext] - go to the next buffer
:bp[revious] - go to the previous buffer
:bd[elete] - delete a buffer (close a file)
:b[uffer]# - go to a buffer by index #
:b[uffer] file - go to a buffer by file
:ls or :buffers - list all open buffers
:sp[lit] file - open a file in a new buffer and split window
:vs[plit] file - open a file in a new buffer and vertically split window
:vert[ical] ba[ll] - edit all buffers as vertical windows
:tab ba[ll] - edit all buffers as tabs
Ctrl + ws - split window
Ctrl + wv - split window vertically
Ctrl + ww - switch windows
Ctrl + wq - quit a window
Ctrl + wx - exchange current window with next one
Ctrl + w= - make all windows equal height &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; width
Ctrl + wh - move cursor to the left window (vertical split)
Ctrl + wl - move cursor to the right window (vertical split)
Ctrl + wj - move cursor to the window below (horizontal split)
Ctrl + wk - move cursor to the window above (horizontal split)
Ctrl + wH - make current window full height at far left (leftmost vertical window)
Ctrl + wL - make current window full height at far right (rightmost vertical window)
Ctrl + wJ - make current window full width at the very bottom (bottommost horizontal window)
Ctrl + wK - make current window full width at the very top (topmost horizontal window)

Diff

zf - manually define a fold up to motion
zd - delete fold under the cursor
za - toggle fold under the cursor
zo - open fold under the cursor
zc - close fold under the cursor
zr - reduce (open) all folds by one level
zm - fold more (close) all folds by one level
zi - toggle folding functionality
]c - jump to start of next change
[c - jump to start of previous change
do or :diffg[et] - obtain (get) difference (from other buffer)
dp or :diffpu[t] - put difference (to other buffer)
:diffthis - make current window part of diff
:dif[fupdate] - update differences
:diffo[ff] - switch off diff mode for current window

# ~/.bashrc: executed by bash(1) for non-login shells.
# see /usr/share/doc/bash/examples/startup-files (in the package bash-doc)
# for examples

# If not running interactively, don&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t do anything
case $- in
    *i*) ;;
      *) return;;
esac

# don&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t put duplicate lines or lines starting with space in the history.
# See bash(1) for more options
HISTCONTROL=ignoreboth

# append to the history file, don&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t overwrite it
shopt -s histappend

# for setting history length see HISTSIZE and HISTFILESIZE in bash(1)
HISTSIZE=1000
HISTFILESIZE=2000

# check the window size after each command and, if necessary,
# update the values of LINES and COLUMNS.
shopt -s checkwinsize

# If set, the pattern &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;**&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; used in a pathname expansion context will
# match all files and zero or more directories and subdirectories.
#shopt -s globstar

# make less more friendly for non-text input files, see lesspipe(1)
[ -x /usr/bin/lesspipe ] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; eval &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$(SHELL=/bin/sh lesspipe)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

# set variable identifying the chroot you work in (used in the prompt below)
if [ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${debian_chroot:-}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; [ -r /etc/debian_chroot ]; then
    debian_chroot=$(cat /etc/debian_chroot)
fi

# disable color support of ls and grep
alias ls=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;ls --color=never&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
alias grep=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;grep --color=never&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
alias fgrep=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;fgrep --color=never&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
alias egrep=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;egrep --color=never&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;

# some more ls aliases
alias ll=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;ls -alF&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
alias la=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;ls -A&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;
alias l=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;ls -CF&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;

# Add an &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;alert&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; alias for long running commands.  Use like so:
#   sleep 10; alert
alias alert=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;notify-send --urgency=low -i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$([ $? = 0 ] &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; echo terminal || echo error)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$(history|tail -n1|sed -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/^\s*[0-9]\+\s*//;s/[;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;|]\s*alert$//&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;

# Alias definitions.
# You may want to put all your additions into a separate file like
# ~/.bash_aliases, instead of adding them here directly.
# See /usr/share/doc/bash-doc/examples in the bash-doc package.

if [ -f ~/.bash_aliases ]; then
    . ~/.bash_aliases
fi

# enable programmable completion features (you don&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t need to enable
# this, if it&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s already enabled in /etc/bash.bashrc and /etc/profile
# sources /etc/bash.bashrc).
if ! shopt -oq posix; then
  if [ -f /usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion ]; then
    . /usr/share/bash-completion/bash_completion
  elif [ -f /etc/bash_completion ]; then
    . /etc/bash_completion
  fi
fi

source ~/bash.library


source ~/bashrc.shared


export JAVA_HOME=/home/mestes/jdk-23.0.2
export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
mkdir -p                     ~/BACKUPS
backup_file   .bashrc        ~/BACKUPS
backup_file   bashrc.shared  ~/BACKUPS
backup_file   bash.library   ~/BACKUPS
backup_file   .vimrc         ~/BACKUPS

                &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Indent and Tab  Setup
                &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; *************************************************************************************
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; There are in fact four main methods available for indentation, each one
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; overrides the previous if it is enabled, or non-empty for &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;indentexpr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;:
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;autoindent&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;  uses the indent from the previous line.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               When opening a new line and no filetype-specific indenting is enabled, keep same
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               indent as line currently on.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;smartindent&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; is like &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;autoindent&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; but also recognizes some C syntax to
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       increase/reduce the indent where appropriate.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;cindent&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; Works more cleverly than the other two and is configurable to
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       different indenting styles.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;indentexpr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;  The most flexible of all: Evaluates an expression to compute
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       the indent of a line.  When non-empty this method overrides
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       the other ones.  See |indent-expression|.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; set cindent                       
set tabstop=4 softtabstop=4
set shiftwidth=4     &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Indent settings for using 4 spaces instead of tabs.
                     &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Do not change &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;tabstop&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; from its default value of 8

    if ( argc() == 1 )

         if (s:n&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;0)
             let $VIMFIRSTFILE=argv(0)
             let s:temp = argv(0)
             let s:temp = substitute(s:temp, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;.vimsession$&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
             let $VIMSESSION=s:temp
             let $VIMWINDOW=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;NIL&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
             let $VIMSPLIT=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;NIL&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
             if ( 1 == 1 )

                 &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;autocmd VimEnter * :echom &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;POPEYE&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    endif

function! MultiToggle()
    let sMt=[]
    call add(sMt, [0, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Upper Mode&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,                  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;:call ToUpperUnderCursor()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [1, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Lower Mode&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,                  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;:call ToLowerUnderCursor()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [2, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;ls&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,                          &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;:ls&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [3 ,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Edit dots and configs&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,       &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;:call EditDotFiles()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [4, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Open Vim Sheatsheet&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,         &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;:e ~/.vim/vimbrief.txt&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [5, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Reselect Visual Selection&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,   &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;gv&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [6, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Search for Word Under Cursor&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;:%s/\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;C-r&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;C-w&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;//gI&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;Left&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;Left&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;Left&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [6, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;6One&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Two&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [7, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;7One&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Two&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    call add(sMt, [8, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;8TestMeMe&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;silent nnoremap  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call g:Test()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ])
    call add(sMt, [9, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;9One&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Two&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;])
    let g:multi_toggle_state = g:multi_toggle_state  + 1
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 7
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 0
    endif
    execute &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;silent nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; . sMt[g:multi_toggle_state][2]
    let &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;statusline = sMt[g:multi_toggle_state][1]
endfunction

function! ToLowerUnderCursor()
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Get the current cursor position.
  let [row, col] = getpos(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;)[1:2]

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Get the character under the cursor.
  let char = getline(row)[col-1]

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Check if a character exists at the cursor position (not end of line).
  if char != &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Convert the character to lowercase.
    let lower_char = tolower(char)

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Replace the character under the cursor with the lowercase version.
    call setline(row, strpart(getline(row), 0, col-1) . lower_char . strpart(getline(row), col))

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Restore the cursor position (important!).
    call cursor(row, col)
  endif
endfunction
function! ToUpperUnderCursor()
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Get the current cursor position.
  let [row, col] = getpos(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;)[1:2]

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Get the character under the cursor.
  let char = getline(row)[col-1]

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Check if a character exists at the cursor position (not end of line).
  if char != &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Convert the character to uppercase.
    let upper_char = toupper(char)

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Replace the character under the cursor with the uppercase version.
    call setline(row, strpart(getline(row), 0, col-1) . upper_char . strpart(getline(row), col))

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Restore the cursor position (important!).
    call cursor(row, col)
  endif
endfunction

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; hello
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
