function! MultiToggle()
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 1
        nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call ToUpperUnderCursor()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Upper Mode&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 2
        return
    endif
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 2
        nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call ToLowerUnderCursor()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Lower Mode&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 3
        return
    endif
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 3
        nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; gv
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Re-Select Visual Mode (gv)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 4
        return
    endif
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 4
        nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :%s/\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;C-r&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;C-w&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;//gI&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;Left&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;Left&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;Left&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Search Word Under Cursor Mode&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 5
        return
    endif
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 5
        nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; : e ~/.vim/vimbrief.txt&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Open Vim Cheatsheet Mode &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; . $HOME . &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;/.vim/vimbrief.txt&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 6
        return
    endif
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 6
        nnoremap         &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call g:FlashCard($HOME . &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;/.vim/1.fc&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call g:UnFlashCard()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Flash Card Mode&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 7
        return
    endif
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 7
        nnoremap         &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call EditDotFiles()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Edit dots and Configs&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 8
        return
    endif
    if g:multi_toggle_state == 8
        nnoremap         &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call DisplayFileReadonlyPopup(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;/tmp/zed&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Test&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 9
        return
    endif


    if g:multi_toggle_state == 9
        nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call MultiToggleVoid()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
        call s:SLine(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Void Mode&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
        let g:multi_toggle_state = 1
        return
    endif
endfunction

function! EditDotFiles()
        execute  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;edit ~/.bashrc&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
        execute  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;edit ~/.vimrc&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
        execute  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;edit ~/.profile&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
        execute  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;edit ~/.vim/vimbrief.txt&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
        execute  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;edit ~/.vim/vim.txt&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
endfunction
function! MultiToggleVoid()
        let g:multi_toggle_state = g:multi_toggle_state = 2
endfunction

let g:multi_toggle_state = 1
let &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;statusline = &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Void Mode&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F7&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call MultiToggleVoid()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F8&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; :call MultiToggle()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

function! ToLowerUnderCursor()
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Get the current cursor position.
  let [row, col] = getpos(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;)[1:2]

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Get the character under the cursor.
  let char = getline(row)[col-1]

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Check if a character exists at the cursor position (not end of line).
  if char != &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Convert the character to lowercase.
    let lower_char = tolower(char)

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Replace the character under the cursor with the lowercase version.
    call setline(row, strpart(getline(row), 0, col-1) . lower_char . strpart(getline(row), col))

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Restore the cursor position (important!).
    call cursor(row, col)
  endif
endfunction
function! ToUpperUnderCursor()
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Get the current cursor position.
  let [row, col] = getpos(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;)[1:2]

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Get the character under the cursor.
  let char = getline(row)[col-1]

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Check if a character exists at the cursor position (not end of line).
  if char != &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Convert the character to uppercase.
    let upper_char = toupper(char)

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Replace the character under the cursor with the uppercase version.
    call setline(row, strpart(getline(row), 0, col-1) . upper_char . strpart(getline(row), col))

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Restore the cursor position (important!).
    call cursor(row, col)
  endif
endfunction

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Map a key to call the function.  For example, map &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;Leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;u to it.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; You can choose any key combination you prefer.  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;Leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; is often \.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; See :help leader for more about setting the leader key.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Example:
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; hello
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Option 1: Add the current file
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;gaf :!git add %&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Option 2: Add the current file and stage changes
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;gac :!git add % &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; git commit -m &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Staged changes&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Option 3: Add all changes in the current directory
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;gaa :!git add .&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Option 4: Add all changes in the current directory and stage changes
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;gss :!git add . &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; git commit -m &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Staged all changes&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Option 5: Add the current file and show git status
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;gas :!git add %&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;:!git status&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Option 6: Add all changes in the current directory and show git status
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;gaas :!git add .&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;:!git status&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Option 7: Add the current file and run a custom git command
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;gac :!git add % &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; git commit -m &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;C-r&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;=@%&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Option 8: Add all changes in the current directory and run a custom git command
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;gacc :!git add . &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; git commit -m &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;C-r&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;=getcwd()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;



function! DisplayFileReadonlyPopup(filepath)
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Check if the file exists and is readable
  if !filereadable(a:filepath)
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;File not found or not readable: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; . a:filepath
    return
  endif

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Create a new buffer for the popup
  silent new
  let bufnum = bufnr(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Set options for the buffer (readonly, no swap, no undo, no list in buffers)
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;setlocal readonly noswapfile nobuflisted noundofile nowindow
  setlocal readonly noswapfile

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Read the file contents into the buffer
  silent execute &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;read &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; . a:filepath

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Open the popup window.  Adjust width and height as needed.
  call popup_create(bufnum, { &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;title&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: fnamemodify(a:filepath, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;:t&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;),&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;line&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;col&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;width&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 80,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;height&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 20,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;scrollbar&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1,&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;border&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;wrap&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1})

  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Store the popup ID in the buffer so we can close it later
  let b:popup_id = popup_getid()

endfunction

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;    call popup_create(bufnum, {
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;title&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: fnamemodify(a:filepath, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;:t&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;),
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;line&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1,
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;col&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1,
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;width&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 80,
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;height&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 20,
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;scrollbar&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1,
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;border&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1,
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;wrap&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: 1,
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;close&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;any&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;,
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      \ })
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Example mapping to display the current file in a popup
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;pf :call DisplayFileReadonlyPopup(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%:p&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Example mapping to display a specific file in a popup
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;po :call DisplayFileReadonlyPopup(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;path/to/my/file.txt&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Replace with your path

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Example command to display a file
command! -nargs=1 DisplayFileReadonlyPopup :call DisplayFileReadonlyPopup(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;q-args&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;)

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Function to close the popup
function! CloseReadonlyPopup()
  if exists(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;b:popup_id&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;) &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; popup_exists(b:popup_id)
    call popup_close(b:popup_id)
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Clean up the buffer - optional, but good practice
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; execute &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;bwipeout &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; . bufnr(&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;%&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
    unlet b:popup_id
  endif
endfunction

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Example mapping to close the popup
nnoremap &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;leader&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;pc :call CloseReadonlyPopup()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;CR&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Autocommand to close the popup when the buffer is closed.
autocmd BufUnload * call CloseReadonlyPopup()

Processing file: output.txt
             _               _    _        _

                |_|                            
Global
:h[elp] keyword - open help for keyword
:sav[eas] file - save file as
:clo[se] - close current pane
:ter[minal] - open a terminal window
K - open man page for word under the cursor
Tip Run vimtutor in a terminal to learn the first Vim commands.
Cursor movement
h - move cursor left
j - move cursor down
k - move cursor up
l - move cursor right
gj - move cursor down (multi-line text)
gk - move cursor up (multi-line text)
H - move to top of screen
M - move to middle of screen
L - move to bottom of screen
w - jump forwards to the start of a word
W - jump forwards to the start of a word (words can contain punctuation)
e - jump forwards to the end of a word
E - jump forwards to the end of a word (words can contain punctuation)
b - jump backwards to the start of a word
B - jump backwards to the start of a word (words can contain punctuation)
ge - jump backwards to the end of a word
gE - jump backwards to the end of a word (words can contain punctuation)
% - move cursor to matching character (default supported pairs: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;{}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;[]&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; 
- use :h matchpairs in vim for more info)
0 - jump to the start of the line
^ - jump to the first non-blank character of the line
$ - jump to the end of the line
g_ - jump to the last non-blank character of the line
gg - go to the first line of the document
G - go to the last line of the document
5gg or 5G - go to line 5
gd - move to local declaration
gD - move to global declaration
fx - jump to next occurrence of character x
tx - jump to before next occurrence of character x
Fx - jump to the previous occurrence of character x
Tx - jump to after previous occurrence of character x
; - repeat previous f, t, F or T movement
, - repeat previous f, t, F or T movement, backwards
} - jump to next paragraph (or function/block, when editing code)
{ - jump to previous paragraph (or function/block, when editing code)
zz - center cursor on screen
zt - position cursor on top of the screen
zb - position cursor on bottom of the screen
Ctrl + e - move screen down one line (without moving cursor)
Ctrl + y - move screen up one line (without moving cursor)
Ctrl + b - move screen up one page (cursor to last line)
Ctrl + f - move screen down one page (cursor to first line)
Ctrl + d - move cursor and screen down 1/2 page
Ctrl + u - move cursor and screen up 1/2 page
Insert mode - inserting/appending text
i - insert before the cursor
I - insert at the beginning of the line
a - insert (append) after the cursor
A - insert (append) at the end of the line
o - append (open) a new line below the current line
O - append (open) a new line above the current line
ea - insert (append) at the end of the word
Ctrl + h - delete the character before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + w - delete word before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + j - add a line break at the cursor position during insert mode
Ctrl + t - indent (move right) line one shiftwidth during insert mode
Ctrl + d - de-indent (move left) line one shiftwidth during insert mode
Ctrl + n - insert (auto-complete) next match before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + p - insert (auto-complete) previous match before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + rx - insert the contents of register x
Ctrl + ox - Temporarily enter normal mode to issue one normal-mode command x.
Esc or Ctrl + c - exit insert mode
Editing
r - replace a single character.
R - replace more than one character, until ESC is pressed.
J - join line below to the current one with one space in between
gJ - join line below to the current one without space in between
gwip - reflow paragraph
g~ - switch case up to motion
gu - change to lowercase up to motion
gU - change to uppercase up to motion
cc - change (replace) entire line
c$ or C - change (replace) to the end of the line
ciw - change (replace) entire word
cw or ce - change (replace) to the end of the word
s - delete character and substitute text (same as cl)
S - delete line and substitute text (same as cc)
xp - transpose two letters (delete and paste)
u - undo
U - restore (undo) last changed line
Ctrl + r - redo
. - repeat last command
Marking text (visual mode)
v - start visual mode, mark lines, then do a command (like y-yank)
V - start linewise visual mode
o - move to other end of marked area
Ctrl + v - start visual block mode
O - move to other corner of block
aw - mark a word
ab - a block with ()
aB - a block with {}
at - a block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
ib - inner block with ()
iB - inner block with {}
it - inner block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
Esc or Ctrl + c - exit visual mode
Visual commands
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; - shift text right
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; - shift text left
y - yank (copy) marked text
d - delete marked text
~ - switch case
u - change marked text to lowercase
U - change marked text to uppercase
Registers
:reg[isters] - show registers content
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;xy - yank into register x
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;xp - paste contents of register x
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;+y - yank into the system clipboard register
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;+p - paste from the system clipboard register
Tip Registers are being stored in ~/.viminfo, and will be loaded again on next restart of vim.
Special registers:
0 - last yank
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; - unnamed register, last delete or yank
% - current file name
# - alternate file name
* - clipboard contents (X11 primary)
+ - clipboard contents (X11 clipboard)
/ - last search pattern
: - last command-line
. - last inserted text
- - last small (less than a line) delete
= - expression register
_ - black hole register
Marks and positions
:marks - list of marks
ma - set current position for mark A
`a - jump to position of mark A
y`a - yank text to position of mark A
`0 - go to the position where Vim was previously exited
`&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; - go to the position when last editing this file
`. - go to the position of the last change in this file
`` - go to the position before the last jump
:ju[mps] - list of jumps
Ctrl + i - go to newer position in jump list
Ctrl + o - go to older position in jump list
:changes - list of changes
g, - go to newer position in change list
g; - go to older position in change list
Ctrl + ] - jump to the tag under cursor
Tip To jump to a mark you can either use a backtick (`) or an apostrophe (&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;).
Using an apostrophe jumps to the beginning (first non-blank) of the line holding the mark.
Macros
qa - record macro a
q - stop recording macro
@a - run macro a
@@ - rerun last run macro
Cut and paste
yy - yank (copy) a line
2yy - yank (copy) 2 lines
yw - yank (copy) the characters of the word from the cursor position to the start of the next word
yiw - yank (copy) word under the cursor
yaw - yank (copy) word under the cursor and the space after or before it
y$ or Y - yank (copy) to end of line
p - put (paste) the clipboard after cursor
P - put (paste) before cursor
gp - put (paste) the clipboard after cursor and leave cursor after the new text
gP - put (paste) before cursor and leave cursor after the new text
dd - delete (cut) a line
2dd - delete (cut) 2 lines
dw - delete (cut) the characters of the word from the cursor position to the start of the next word
diw - delete (cut) word under the cursor
daw - delete (cut) word under the cursor and the space after or before it
:3,5d - delete lines starting from 3 to 5
Tip You can also use the following characters to specify the range:
e.g.
:.,$d - From the current line to the end of the file
:.,1d - From the current line to the beginning of the file
:10,1d - From the 10th line to the beginning of the file
:g/{pattern}/d - delete all lines containing pattern
:g!/{pattern}/d - delete all lines not containing pattern
d$ or D - delete (cut) to the end of the line
x - delete (cut) character
Indent text
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; - indent (move right) line one shiftwidth
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; - de-indent (move left) line one shiftwidth
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;% - indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;% - de-indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;ib - indent inner block with ()
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;at - indent a block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
3== - re-indent 3 lines
=% - re-indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
=iB - re-indent inner block with {}
gg=G - re-indent entire buffer
]p - paste and adjust indent to current line
Exiting
:w - write (save) the file, but don&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t exit
:w !sudo tee % - write out the current file using sudo
:wq or :x or ZZ - write (save) and quit
:q - quit (fails if there are unsaved changes)
:q! or ZQ - quit and throw away unsaved changes
:wqa - write (save) and quit on all tabs
Search and replace
/pattern - search for pattern
?pattern - search backward for pattern
\vpattern - &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;very magic&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; pattern: non-alphanumeric characters are interpreted as special regex symbols (no escaping needed)
n - repeat search in same direction
N - repeat search in opposite direction
:%s/old/new/g - replace all old with new throughout file
:%s/old/new/gc - replace all old with new throughout file with confirmations
:noh[lsearch] - remove highlighting of search matches
Search in multiple files
:vim[grep] /pattern/ {`{file}`} - search for pattern in multiple files
e.g. :vim[grep] /foo/ **/*
:cn[ext] - jump to the next match
:cp[revious] - jump to the previous match
:cope[n] - open a window containing the list of matches
:ccl[ose] - close the quickfix window
Tabs
:tabnew or :tabnew {page.words.file} - open a file in a new tab
Ctrl + wT - move the current split window into its own tab
gt or :tabn[ext] - move to the next tab
gT or :tabp[revious] - move to the previous tab
#gt - move to tab number #
:tabm[ove] # - move current tab to the #th position (indexed from 0)
:tabc[lose] - close the current tab and all its windows
:tabo[nly] - close all tabs except for the current one
:tabdo command - run the command on all tabs (e.g. :tabdo q - closes all opened tabs)
Working with multiple files
:e[dit] file - edit a file in a new buffer
:bn[ext] - go to the next buffer
:bp[revious] - go to the previous buffer
:bd[elete] - delete a buffer (close a file)
:b[uffer]# - go to a buffer by index #
:b[uffer] file - go to a buffer by file
:ls or :buffers - list all open buffers
:sp[lit] file - open a file in a new buffer and split window
:vs[plit] file - open a file in a new buffer and vertically split window
:vert[ical] ba[ll] - edit all buffers as vertical windows
:tab ba[ll] - edit all buffers as tabs
Ctrl + ws - split window
Ctrl + wv - split window vertically
Ctrl + ww - switch windows
Ctrl + wq - quit a window
Ctrl + wx - exchange current window with next one
Ctrl + w= - make all windows equal height &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; width
Ctrl + wh - move cursor to the left window (vertical split)
Ctrl + wl - move cursor to the right window (vertical split)
Ctrl + wj - move cursor to the window below (horizontal split)
Ctrl + wk - move cursor to the window above (horizontal split)
Ctrl + wH - make current window full height at far left (leftmost vertical window)
Ctrl + wL - make current window full height at far right (rightmost vertical window)
Ctrl + wJ - make current window full width at the very bottom (bottommost horizontal window)
Ctrl + wK - make current window full width at the very top (topmost horizontal window)
Diff
zf - manually define a fold up to motion
zd - delete fold under the cursor
za - toggle fold under the cursor
zo - open fold under the cursor
zc - close fold under the cursor
zr - reduce (open) all folds by one level
zm - fold more (close) all folds by one level
zi - toggle folding functionality
]c - jump to start of next change
[c - jump to start of previous change
do or :diffg[et] - obtain (get) difference (from other buffer)
dp or :diffpu[t] - put difference (to other buffer)
:diffthis - make current window part of diff
:dif[fupdate] - update differences
:diffo[ff] - switch off diff mode for current window

rm -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$Tmp1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;/dev/null 2&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;1

filename=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Usage: $0 &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  exit 1
fi

# Check if the file exists
if [ ! -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: File &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; not found.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  exit 1
fi

backup_file  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;   ~/BACKUPS

sed &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;s/[[:space:]]*$//&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; $Tmp

# Find the longest line length
max_len=$(wc -L &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$Tmp&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; | awk &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;{print $1}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;)

# Calculate the padding length
padding_length=$((max_len + 1))

# Create a temporary file to store the padded content
temp_file=$(mktemp)

# Iterate through each line of the file and pad it
while IFS= read -r line; do

done  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$Tmp&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

# Replace the original file with the padded content
cat &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$temp_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;   &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

# echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;File &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$filename&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; padded successfully.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

create_markdown_table() {
  local input_file=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  # Check if the input file exists
  if [[ ! -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Error: Input file &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; not found.&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    return 1
  fi

  # Read lines from the file and create table rows
  local line_count=0
  local row=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  local first_row=1

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    if [[ $line_count -eq 0 ]]; then
      if [[ $first_row -eq 1 ]]; then
          #echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 | Column 4 | Column 5 | Column 6 |&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
          echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;|    A     |    B     |    C     |    D     |    E     |&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
          echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
          first_row=0
      fi
    fi

    row+=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;| $line &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

    line_count=$((line_count + 1))

    if [[ $line_count -eq 5 ]]; then
      echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$row|&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
      row=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
      line_count=0
    fi
  done &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;

  # Handle remaining lines if the total line count is not a multiple of 5
  if [[ $line_count -gt 0 ]]; then
    for ((i = line_count; i &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; 5; i++)); do
        row+=&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;|  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    done
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$row|&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
  fi
}

    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; *********************************************************DATEOMATIC: $D&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;      &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; $Tmp1
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;\&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; *********************************************************HASHOMATIC: $IHASH&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; $Tmp1
    cat $Tmp  &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; $Tmp1

    git add &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$FILE&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
fi

Global

:h[elp] keyword - open help for keyword
:sav[eas] file - save file as
:clo[se] - close current pane
:ter[minal] - open a terminal window
K - open man page for word under the cursor
Tip Run vimtutor in a terminal to learn the first Vim commands.

Cursor movement

h - move cursor left
j - move cursor down
k - move cursor up
l - move cursor right
gj - move cursor down (multi-line text)
gk - move cursor up (multi-line text)
H - move to top of screen
M - move to middle of screen
L - move to bottom of screen
w - jump forwards to the start of a word
W - jump forwards to the start of a word (words can contain punctuation)
e - jump forwards to the end of a word
E - jump forwards to the end of a word (words can contain punctuation)
b - jump backwards to the start of a word
B - jump backwards to the start of a word (words can contain punctuation)
ge - jump backwards to the end of a word
gE - jump backwards to the end of a word (words can contain punctuation)
% - move cursor to matching character (default supported pairs: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;()&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;{}&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;[]&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; 
- use :h matchpairs in vim for more info)
0 - jump to the start of the line
^ - jump to the first non-blank character of the line
$ - jump to the end of the line
g_ - jump to the last non-blank character of the line
gg - go to the first line of the document
G - go to the last line of the document
5gg or 5G - go to line 5
gd - move to local declaration
gD - move to global declaration
fx - jump to next occurrence of character x
tx - jump to before next occurrence of character x
Fx - jump to the previous occurrence of character x
Tx - jump to after previous occurrence of character x
; - repeat previous f, t, F or T movement
, - repeat previous f, t, F or T movement, backwards
} - jump to next paragraph (or function/block, when editing code)
{ - jump to previous paragraph (or function/block, when editing code)
zz - center cursor on screen
zt - position cursor on top of the screen
zb - position cursor on bottom of the screen
Ctrl + e - move screen down one line (without moving cursor)
Ctrl + y - move screen up one line (without moving cursor)
Ctrl + b - move screen up one page (cursor to last line)
Ctrl + f - move screen down one page (cursor to first line)
Ctrl + d - move cursor and screen down 1/2 page
Ctrl + u - move cursor and screen up 1/2 page

Insert mode - inserting/appending text

i - insert before the cursor
I - insert at the beginning of the line
a - insert (append) after the cursor
A - insert (append) at the end of the line
o - append (open) a new line below the current line
O - append (open) a new line above the current line
ea - insert (append) at the end of the word
Ctrl + h - delete the character before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + w - delete word before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + j - add a line break at the cursor position during insert mode
Ctrl + t - indent (move right) line one shiftwidth during insert mode
Ctrl + d - de-indent (move left) line one shiftwidth during insert mode
Ctrl + n - insert (auto-complete) next match before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + p - insert (auto-complete) previous match before the cursor during insert mode
Ctrl + rx - insert the contents of register x
Ctrl + ox - Temporarily enter normal mode to issue one normal-mode command x.
Esc or Ctrl + c - exit insert mode

Editing

r - replace a single character.
R - replace more than one character, until ESC is pressed.
J - join line below to the current one with one space in between
gJ - join line below to the current one without space in between
gwip - reflow paragraph
g~ - switch case up to motion
gu - change to lowercase up to motion
gU - change to uppercase up to motion
cc - change (replace) entire line
c$ or C - change (replace) to the end of the line
ciw - change (replace) entire word
cw or ce - change (replace) to the end of the word
s - delete character and substitute text (same as cl)
S - delete line and substitute text (same as cc)
xp - transpose two letters (delete and paste)
u - undo
U - restore (undo) last changed line
Ctrl + r - redo
. - repeat last command

Marking text (visual mode)

v - start visual mode, mark lines, then do a command (like y-yank)
V - start linewise visual mode
o - move to other end of marked area
Ctrl + v - start visual block mode
O - move to other corner of block
aw - mark a word
ab - a block with ()
aB - a block with {}
at - a block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
ib - inner block with ()
iB - inner block with {}
it - inner block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
Esc or Ctrl + c - exit visual mode

Visual commands

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; - shift text right
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; - shift text left
y - yank (copy) marked text
d - delete marked text
~ - switch case
u - change marked text to lowercase
U - change marked text to uppercase

Registers

:reg[isters] - show registers content
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;xy - yank into register x
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;xp - paste contents of register x
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;+y - yank into the system clipboard register
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;+p - paste from the system clipboard register
Tip Registers are being stored in ~/.viminfo, and will be loaded again on next restart of vim.

Special registers:

0 - last yank
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; - unnamed register, last delete or yank
% - current file name
# - alternate file name
* - clipboard contents (X11 primary)
+ - clipboard contents (X11 clipboard)
/ - last search pattern
: - last command-line
. - last inserted text
- - last small (less than a line) delete
= - expression register
_ - black hole register

Marks and positions

:marks - list of marks
ma - set current position for mark A
`a - jump to position of mark A
y`a - yank text to position of mark A
`0 - go to the position where Vim was previously exited
`&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; - go to the position when last editing this file
`. - go to the position of the last change in this file
`` - go to the position before the last jump
:ju[mps] - list of jumps
Ctrl + i - go to newer position in jump list
Ctrl + o - go to older position in jump list
:changes - list of changes
g, - go to newer position in change list
g; - go to older position in change list
Ctrl + ] - jump to the tag under cursor
Tip To jump to a mark you can either use a backtick (`) or an apostrophe (&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;).
Using an apostrophe jumps to the beginning (first non-blank) of the line holding the mark.

Macros

qa - record macro a
q - stop recording macro
@a - run macro a
@@ - rerun last run macro

Cut and paste

yy - yank (copy) a line
2yy - yank (copy) 2 lines
yw - yank (copy) the characters of the word from the cursor position to the start of the next word
yiw - yank (copy) word under the cursor
yaw - yank (copy) word under the cursor and the space after or before it
y$ or Y - yank (copy) to end of line
p - put (paste) the clipboard after cursor
P - put (paste) before cursor
gp - put (paste) the clipboard after cursor and leave cursor after the new text
gP - put (paste) before cursor and leave cursor after the new text
dd - delete (cut) a line
2dd - delete (cut) 2 lines
dw - delete (cut) the characters of the word from the cursor position to the start of the next word
diw - delete (cut) word under the cursor
daw - delete (cut) word under the cursor and the space after or before it
:3,5d - delete lines starting from 3 to 5
Tip You can also use the following characters to specify the range:
e.g.
:.,$d - From the current line to the end of the file
:.,1d - From the current line to the beginning of the file
:10,1d - From the 10th line to the beginning of the file
:g/{pattern}/d - delete all lines containing pattern
:g!/{pattern}/d - delete all lines not containing pattern
d$ or D - delete (cut) to the end of the line
x - delete (cut) character

Indent text

&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; - indent (move right) line one shiftwidth
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; - de-indent (move left) line one shiftwidth
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;% - indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;% - de-indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;ib - indent inner block with ()
&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;at - indent a block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
3== - re-indent 3 lines
=% - re-indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
=iB - re-indent inner block with {}
gg=G - re-indent entire buffer
]p - paste and adjust indent to current line

Exiting

:w - write (save) the file, but don&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t exit
:w !sudo tee % - write out the current file using sudo
:wq or :x or ZZ - write (save) and quit
:q - quit (fails if there are unsaved changes)
:q! or ZQ - quit and throw away unsaved changes
:wqa - write (save) and quit on all tabs

Search and replace

/pattern - search for pattern
?pattern - search backward for pattern
\vpattern - &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;very magic&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; pattern: non-alphanumeric characters are interpreted as special regex symbols (no escaping needed)
n - repeat search in same direction
N - repeat search in opposite direction
:%s/old/new/g - replace all old with new throughout file
:%s/old/new/gc - replace all old with new throughout file with confirmations
:noh[lsearch] - remove highlighting of search matches

Search in multiple files

:vim[grep] /pattern/ {`{file}`} - search for pattern in multiple files
e.g. :vim[grep] /foo/ **/*
:cn[ext] - jump to the next match
:cp[revious] - jump to the previous match
:cope[n] - open a window containing the list of matches
:ccl[ose] - close the quickfix window

Tabs

:tabnew or :tabnew {page.words.file} - open a file in a new tab
Ctrl + wT - move the current split window into its own tab
gt or :tabn[ext] - move to the next tab
gT or :tabp[revious] - move to the previous tab
#gt - move to tab number #
:tabm[ove] # - move current tab to the #th position (indexed from 0)
:tabc[lose] - close the current tab and all its windows
:tabo[nly] - close all tabs except for the current one
:tabdo command - run the command on all tabs (e.g. :tabdo q - closes all opened tabs)

Working with multiple files

:e[dit] file - edit a file in a new buffer
:bn[ext] - go to the next buffer

:bd[elete] - delete a buffer (close a file)
:b[uffer]# - go to a buffer by index #
:b[uffer] file - go to a buffer by file
:ls or :buffers - list all open buffers
:sp[lit] file - open a file in a new buffer and split window
:vs[plit] file - open a file in a new buffer and vertically split window
:vert[ical] ba[ll] - edit all buffers as vertical windows
:tab ba[ll] - edit all buffers as tabs
Ctrl + ws - split window
Ctrl + wv - split window vertically
Ctrl + ww - switch windows
Ctrl + wq - quit a window
Ctrl + wx - exchange current window with next one
Ctrl + w= - make all windows equal height &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; width
Ctrl + wh - move cursor to the left window (vertical split)
Ctrl + wl - move cursor to the right window (vertical split)
Ctrl + wj - move cursor to the window below (horizontal split)
Ctrl + wk - move cursor to the window above (horizontal split)
Ctrl + wH - make current window full height at far left (leftmost vertical window)
Ctrl + wL - make current window full height at far right (rightmost vertical window)
Ctrl + wJ - make current window full width at the very bottom (bottommost horizontal window)
Ctrl + wK - make current window full width at the very top (topmost horizontal window)

Diff

zf - manually define a fold up to motion

zc - close fold under the cursor

dp or :diffpu[t] - put difference (to other buffer)
:diffthis - make current window part of diff
:dif[fupdate] - update differences
:diffo[ff] - switch off diff mode for current window

    ^ - jump to the first non-blank character of the line
    $ - jump to the end of the line
    g_ - jump to the last non-blank character of the line
    gg - go to the first line of the document
    G - go to the last line of the document
    5gg or 5G - go to line 5
    gd - move to local declaration
    gD - move to global declaration
    fx - jump to next occurrence of character x
    tx - jump to before next occurrence of character x
    Fx - jump to the previous occurrence of character x
    Tx - jump to after previous occurrence of character x
    ; - repeat previous f, t, F or T movement
    , - repeat previous f, t, F or T movement, backwards
    } - jump to next paragraph (or function/block, when editing code)
    { - jump to previous paragraph (or function/block, when editing code)
    zz - center cursor on screen
    zt - position cursor on top of the screen
    zb - position cursor on bottom of the screen
    Ctrl + e - move screen down one line (without moving cursor)
    Ctrl + y - move screen up one line (without moving cursor)
    Ctrl + b - move screen up one page (cursor to last line)
    Ctrl + f - move screen down one page (cursor to first line)
    Ctrl + d - move cursor and screen down 1/2 page
    Ctrl + u - move cursor and screen up 1/2 page

Insert mode - inserting/appending text

    i - insert before the cursor
    I - insert at the beginning of the line
    a - insert (append) after the cursor
    A - insert (append) at the end of the line
    o - append (open) a new line below the current line
    O - append (open) a new line above the current line
    ea - insert (append) at the end of the word
    Ctrl + h - delete the character before the cursor during insert mode
    Ctrl + w - delete word before the cursor during insert mode
    Ctrl + j - add a line break at the cursor position during insert mode
    Ctrl + t - indent (move right) line one shiftwidth during insert mode
    Ctrl + d - de-indent (move left) line one shiftwidth during insert mode
    Ctrl + n - insert (auto-complete) next match before the cursor during insert mode
    Ctrl + p - insert (auto-complete) previous match before the cursor during insert mode
    Ctrl + rx - insert the contents of register x
    Ctrl + ox - Temporarily enter normal mode to issue one normal-mode command x.
    Esc or Ctrl + c - exit insert mode

Editing

    r - replace a single character.
    R - replace more than one character, until ESC is pressed.
    J - join line below to the current one with one space in between
    gJ - join line below to the current one without space in between
    gwip - reflow paragraph
    g~ - switch case up to motion
    gu - change to lowercase up to motion
    gU - change to uppercase up to motion
    cc - change (replace) entire line
    c$ or C - change (replace) to the end of the line
    ciw - change (replace) entire word
    cw or ce - change (replace) to the end of the word
    s - delete character and substitute text (same as cl)
    S - delete line and substitute text (same as cc)
    xp - transpose two letters (delete and paste)
    u - undo
    U - restore (undo) last changed line
    Ctrl + r - redo
    . - repeat last command

Marking text (visual mode)

    v - start visual mode, mark lines, then do a command (like y-yank)
    V - start linewise visual mode
    o - move to other end of marked area
    Ctrl + v - start visual block mode
    O - move to other corner of block
    aw - mark a word
    ab - a block with ()
    aB - a block with {}
    at - a block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
    ib - inner block with ()
    iB - inner block with {}
    it - inner block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
    Esc or Ctrl + c - exit visual mode

Visual commands

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; - shift text right
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; - shift text left
    y - yank (copy) marked text
    d - delete marked text
    ~ - switch case
    u - change marked text to lowercase
    U - change marked text to uppercase

Registers

    :reg[isters] - show registers content
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;xy - yank into register x
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;xp - paste contents of register x
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;+y - yank into the system clipboard register
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;+p - paste from the system clipboard register
    Tip Registers are being stored in ~/.viminfo, and will be loaded again on next restart of vim.

Special registers:

    0 - last yank
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; - unnamed register, last delete or yank
    % - current file name
    # - alternate file name
    * - clipboard contents (X11 primary)
    + - clipboard contents (X11 clipboard)
    / - last search pattern
    : - last command-line
    . - last inserted text
    - - last small (less than a line) delete
    = - expression register
    _ - black hole register

Marks and positions

    :marks - list of marks
    ma - set current position for mark A
    `a - jump to position of mark A
    y`a - yank text to position of mark A
    `0 - go to the position where Vim was previously exited
    `&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; - go to the position when last editing this file
    `. - go to the position of the last change in this file
    `` - go to the position before the last jump
    :ju[mps] - list of jumps
    Ctrl + i - go to newer position in jump list
    Ctrl + o - go to older position in jump list
    :changes - list of changes
    g, - go to newer position in change list
    g; - go to older position in change list
    Ctrl + ] - jump to the tag under cursor
    Tip To jump to a mark you can either use a backtick (`) or an apostrophe (&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;).
    Using an apostrophe jumps to the beginning (first non-blank) of the line holding the mark.

Macros

    qa - record macro a
    q - stop recording macro
    @a - run macro a
    @@ - rerun last run macro

Cut and paste

    yy - yank (copy) a line
    2yy - yank (copy) 2 lines
    yw - yank (copy) the characters of the word from the cursor position to the start of the next word
    yiw - yank (copy) word under the cursor
    yaw - yank (copy) word under the cursor and the space after or before it
    y$ or Y - yank (copy) to end of line
    p - put (paste) the clipboard after cursor
    P - put (paste) before cursor
    gp - put (paste) the clipboard after cursor and leave cursor after the new text
    gP - put (paste) before cursor and leave cursor after the new text
    dd - delete (cut) a line
    2dd - delete (cut) 2 lines
    dw - delete (cut) the characters of the word from the cursor position to the start of the next word
    diw - delete (cut) word under the cursor
    daw - delete (cut) word under the cursor and the space after or before it
    :3,5d - delete lines starting from 3 to 5
    Tip You can also use the following characters to specify the range:
    e.g.
        :.,$d - From the current line to the end of the file
        :.,1d - From the current line to the beginning of the file
        :10,1d - From the 10th line to the beginning of the file
    :g/{pattern}/d - delete all lines containing pattern
    :g!/{pattern}/d - delete all lines not containing pattern
    d$ or D - delete (cut) to the end of the line
    x - delete (cut) character

Indent text

    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; - indent (move right) line one shiftwidth
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; - de-indent (move left) line one shiftwidth
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;% - indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;% - de-indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;ib - indent inner block with ()
    &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;at - indent a block with &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; tags
    3== - re-indent 3 lines
    =% - re-indent a block with () or {} (cursor on brace)
    =iB - re-indent inner block with {}
    gg=G - re-indent entire buffer
    ]p - paste and adjust indent to current line

Exiting

    :w - write (save) the file, but don&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;t exit
    :w !sudo tee % - write out the current file using sudo
    :wq or :x or ZZ - write (save) and quit
    :q - quit (fails if there are unsaved changes)
    :q! or ZQ - quit and throw away unsaved changes
    :wqa - write (save) and quit on all tabs

Search and replace

    /pattern - search for pattern
    ?pattern - search backward for pattern
    \vpattern - &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;very magic&amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; pattern: non-alphanumeric characters are interpreted as special regex symbols (no escaping needed)
    n - repeat search in same direction
    N - repeat search in opposite direction
    :%s/old/new/g - replace all old with new throughout file
    :%s/old/new/gc - replace all old with new throughout file with confirmations
    :noh[lsearch] - remove highlighting of search matches

Search in multiple files

    :vim[grep] /pattern/ {`{file}`} - search for pattern in multiple files
    e.g. :vim[grep] /foo/ **/*
        :cn[ext] - jump to the next match
        :cp[revious] - jump to the previous match
        :cope[n] - open a window containing the list of matches
        :ccl[ose] - close the quickfix window

Tabs

    :tabnew or :tabnew {page.words.file} - open a file in a new tab
    Ctrl + wT - move the current split window into its own tab
    gt or :tabn[ext] - move to the next tab
    gT or :tabp[revious] - move to the previous tab
    #gt - move to tab number #
    :tabm[ove] # - move current tab to the #th position (indexed from 0)
    :tabc[lose] - close the current tab and all its windows
    :tabo[nly] - close all tabs except for the current one
    :tabdo command - run the command on all tabs (e.g. :tabdo q - closes all opened tabs)

Working with multiple files

    :e[dit] file - edit a file in a new buffer
    :bn[ext] - go to the next buffer
    :bp[revious] - go to the previous buffer
    :bd[elete] - delete a buffer (close a file)
    :b[uffer]# - go to a buffer by index #
    :b[uffer] file - go to a buffer by file
    :ls or :buffers - list all open buffers
    :sp[lit] file - open a file in a new buffer and split window
    :vs[plit] file - open a file in a new buffer and vertically split window
    :vert[ical] ba[ll] - edit all buffers as vertical windows
    :tab ba[ll] - edit all buffers as tabs
    Ctrl + ws - split window
    Ctrl + wv - split window vertically
    Ctrl + ww - switch windows
    Ctrl + wq - quit a window
    Ctrl + wx - exchange current window with next one
    Ctrl + w= - make all windows equal height &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; width
    Ctrl + wh - move cursor to the left window (vertical split)
    Ctrl + wl - move cursor to the right window (vertical split)
    Ctrl + wj - move cursor to the window below (horizontal split)
    Ctrl + wk - move cursor to the window above (horizontal split)
    Ctrl + wH - make current window full height at far left (leftmost vertical window)
    Ctrl + wL - make current window full height at far right (rightmost vertical window)
    Ctrl + wJ - make current window full width at the very bottom (bottommost horizontal window)
    Ctrl + wK - make current window full width at the very top (topmost horizontal window)

Diff

    zf - manually define a fold up to motion
    zd - delete fold under the cursor
    za - toggle fold under the cursor
    zo - open fold under the cursor
    zc - close fold under the cursor
    zr - reduce (open) all folds by one level
    zm - fold more (close) all folds by one level
    zi - toggle folding functionality
    ]c - jump to start of next change
    [c - jump to start of previous change
    do or :diffg[et] - obtain (get) difference (from other buffer)
    dp or :diffpu[t] - put difference (to other buffer)
    :diffthis - make current window part of diff
    :dif[fupdate] - update differences
    :diffo[ff] - switch off diff mode for current window&amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;/code&amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;/pre&amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;
  &amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;/body&amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

.markdown-body details,
.markdown-body figcaption,
.markdown-body figure {
  display: block;
}

.markdown-body summary {
  display: list-item;
}

.markdown-body [hidden] {
  display: none !important;
}

.markdown-body a {
  background-color: transparent;
  color: #4493f8;
  text-decoration: none;
}

.markdown-body abbr[title] {
  border-bottom: none;
  -webkit-text-decoration: underline dotted;
  text-decoration: underline dotted;
}

.markdown-body b,
.markdown-body strong {
  font-weight: 600;
}

.markdown-body dfn {
  font-style: italic;
}

.markdown-body h1 {
  margin: .67em 0;
  font-weight: 600;
  padding-bottom: .3em;
  font-size: 2em;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #3d444db3;
}

.markdown-body mark {
  background-color: #bb800926;
  color: #f0f6fc;
}

.markdown-body small {
  font-size: 90%;
}

.markdown-body sub,
.markdown-body sup {
  font-size: 75%;
  line-height: 0;
  position: relative;
  vertical-align: baseline;
}

.markdown-body sub {
  bottom: -0.25em;
}

.markdown-body sup {
  top: -0.5em;
}

.markdown-body img {
  border-style: none;
  max-width: 100%;
  box-sizing: content-box;
}

.markdown-body code,
.markdown-body kbd,
.markdown-body pre,
.markdown-body samp {
  font-family: monospace;
  font-size: 1em;
}

.markdown-body figure {
  margin: 1em 2.5rem;
}

.markdown-body hr {
  box-sizing: content-box;
  overflow: hidden;
  background: transparent;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #3d444db3;
  height: .25em;
  padding: 0;
  margin: 1.5rem 0;
  background-color: #3d444d;
  border: 0;
}

.markdown-body input {
  font: inherit;
  margin: 0;
  overflow: visible;
  font-family: inherit;
  font-size: inherit;
  line-height: inherit;
}

.markdown-body [type=button],
.markdown-body [type=reset],
.markdown-body [type=submit] {
  -webkit-appearance: button;
  appearance: button;
}

.markdown-body [type=checkbox],
.markdown-body [type=radio] {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  padding: 0;
}

.markdown-body [type=number]::-webkit-inner-spin-button,
.markdown-body [type=number]::-webkit-outer-spin-button {
  height: auto;
}

.markdown-body [type=search]::-webkit-search-cancel-button,
.markdown-body [type=search]::-webkit-search-decoration {
  -webkit-appearance: none;
  appearance: none;
}

.markdown-body ::-webkit-input-placeholder {
  color: inherit;
  opacity: .54;
}

.markdown-body ::-webkit-file-upload-button {
  -webkit-appearance: button;
  appearance: button;
  font: inherit;
}

.markdown-body a:hover {
  text-decoration: underline;
}

.markdown-body ::placeholder {
  color: #9198a1;
  opacity: 1;
}

.markdown-body hr::before {
  display: table;
  content: &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
}

.markdown-body hr::after {
  display: table;
  clear: both;
  content: &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;;
}

.markdown-body table {
  border-spacing: 0;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  display: block;
  width: max-content;
  max-width: 100%;
  overflow: auto;
  font-variant: tabular-nums;
}

.markdown-body td,
.markdown-body th {
  padding: 0;
}

.markdown-body details summary {
  cursor: pointer;
}

.markdown-body a:focus,
.markdown-body [role=button]:focus,
.markdown-body input[type=radio]:focus,
.markdown-body input[type=checkbox]:focus {
  outline: 2px solid #1f6feb;
  outline-offset: -2px;
  box-shadow: none;
}

.markdown-body a:focus:not(:focus-visible),
.markdown-body [role=button]:focus:not(:focus-visible),
.markdown-body input[type=radio]:focus:not(:focus-visible),
.markdown-body input[type=checkbox]:focus:not(:focus-visible) {
  outline: solid 1px transparent;
}

.markdown-body a:focus-visible,
.markdown-body [role=button]:focus-visible,
.markdown-body input[type=radio]:focus-visible,
.markdown-body input[type=checkbox]:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid #1f6feb;
  outline-offset: -2px;
  box-shadow: none;
}

.markdown-body a:not([class]):focus,
.markdown-body a:not([class]):focus-visible,
.markdown-body input[type=radio]:focus,
.markdown-body input[type=radio]:focus-visible,
.markdown-body input[type=checkbox]:focus,
.markdown-body input[type=checkbox]:focus-visible {
  outline-offset: 0;
}

.markdown-body kbd {
  display: inline-block;
  padding: 0.25rem;
  font: 11px ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, Liberation Mono, monospace;
  line-height: 10px;
  color: #f0f6fc;
  vertical-align: middle;
  background-color: #151b23;
  border: solid 1px #3d444db3;
  border-bottom-color: #3d444db3;
  border-radius: 6px;
  box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 #3d444db3;
}

.markdown-body h1,
.markdown-body h2,
.markdown-body h3,
.markdown-body h4,
.markdown-body h5,
.markdown-body h6 {
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  margin-bottom: 1rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  line-height: 1.25;
}

.markdown-body h2 {
  font-weight: 600;
  padding-bottom: .3em;
  font-size: 1.5em;
  border-bottom: 1px solid #3d444db3;
}

.markdown-body h3 {
  font-weight: 600;
  font-size: 1.25em;
}

.markdown-body h4 {
  font-weight: 600;
  font-size: 1em;
}

.markdown-body h5 {
  font-weight: 600;
  font-size: .875em;
}

.markdown-body h6 {
  font-weight: 600;
  font-size: .85em;
  color: #9198a1;
}

.markdown-body p {
  margin-top: 0;
  margin-bottom: 10px;
}

.markdown-body blockquote {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0 1em;
  color: #9198a1;
  border-left: .25em solid #3d444d;
}

.markdown-body ul,
.markdown-body ol {
  margin-top: 0;
  margin-bottom: 0;
  padding-left: 2em;
}

.markdown-body ol ol,
.markdown-body ul ol {
  list-style-type: lower-roman;
}

.markdown-body ul ul ol,
.markdown-body ul ol ol,
.markdown-body ol ul ol,
.markdown-body ol ol ol {
  list-style-type: lower-alpha;
}

.markdown-body dd {

scriptinfo() { head -${SCRIPT_HEADSIZE:-99} ${0} | grep -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;^#-&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; | sed -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;s/^#-//g&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; -e &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;s/\${SCRIPT_NAME}/${SCRIPT_NAME}/g&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;; }

BEGIN {
    NOTHING=0
}
//{
    
}
END {
    NOTHING=0
}&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;

# Check if a file exists
if [ -f &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;/path/to/your/file&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;File exists.&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
else
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;File does not exist.&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
fi

# Check if a directory exists
if [ -d &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;/path/to/your/directory&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Directory exists.&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
else
  echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Directory does not exist.&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
fi

# Check if input file is provided
if [ -z &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;Usage: `basename &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$0&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;` &amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    exit 1
if

# filename munging
input_file=&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;                                                                                         
output_file=&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;${input_file%.*}.html&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
cat &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;  | sed &amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;/^$/d&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; | sort | uniq &amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; $Tmp; cp $Tmp &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
line_count=$(wc -l &amp;amp;amp;amp;lt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$input_file&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
half_lines=$((line_count / 3))

# ifs
if [ &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$num&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; -eq 2 ]; then


isnfs () {                                                                                                                       
    LOCAL=`stat -f -c %T &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$1&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;`                                                                                                   
    if [ &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$LOCAL&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; == &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;nfs&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; ]; then                                                                                               
         RETVAL=&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;YES&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;                                                                                                             
    else                                                                                                                         
         RETVAL=&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;NO&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;                                                                                                              
    fi                                                                                                                           
}

consolebar () {
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;********************************************************************************************&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
}
consolemsg () {
#   consolebar
    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;** $1&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
#   consolebar
    A=$A
}
optconsolemsg () {
#    echo &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;** $1&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
    A=$A
}


while getopts &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;ha:&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; arg
do
    case $arg in
        h) usagefull;
           exit 0;
           ;;
        a) A=&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;$OPTARG&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
           exit 0
           ;;
    esac
done
shift $(($OPTIND - 1))

                &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; *************************************************************************************
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; There are in fact four main methods available for indentation, each one
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; overrides the previous if it is enabled, or non-empty for &amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;indentexpr&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;:
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;autoindent&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;  uses the indent from the previous line.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               When opening a new line and no filetype-specific indenting is enabled, keep same
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;               indent as line currently on.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;smartindent&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; is like &amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;autoindent&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; but also recognizes some C syntax to
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       increase/reduce the indent where appropriate.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;cindent&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39; Works more cleverly than the other two and is configurable to
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       different indenting styles.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;indentexpr&amp;amp;amp;amp;#39;  The most flexible of all: Evaluates an expression to compute
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       the indent of a line.  When non-empty this method overrides
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;       the other ones.  See |indent-expression|.
&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; set cindent

function g:LogMessage(...)
    let l:ret = 0

    let l:messages=[]
    call add(l:messages, a:1)
    call writefile(l:messages, &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;/tmp/vimscript.log&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;a&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
    return l:ret
endfunction

inoremap         &amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;F6&amp;amp;amp;amp;gt; &amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;esc&amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;:call ProgramRun()&amp;amp;amp;amp;lt;cr&amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;

&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; *****************************************************************************************************
                &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; Session Setup
                &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot; *************************************************************************************
if ( 1 == 0 ) 
    if ( argc() == 0 ) 
         augroup VIMAUTOGROUPA
             autocmd!
             autocmd VimEnter * :call LoadSession()
         augroup END
    endif
    if ( argc() == 1 ) 
         let s:n=match(argv(0), &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;vimsession$&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
         if (s:n&amp;amp;amp;amp;gt;0)
             let $VIMFIRSTFILE=argv(0)
             let s:temp = argv(0)
             let s:temp = substitute(s:temp, &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;.vimsession$&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;, &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;)
             let $VIMSESSION=s:temp
             let $VIMWINDOW=&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;NIL&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
             let $VIMSPLIT=&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;NIL&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
             if ( 1 == 1 ) 
             augroup VIMAUTOGROUPB
                 autocmd!
                 autocmd VimEnter * :call LoadSession()
                 &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;autocmd VimEnter * :echom &amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;POPEYE&amp;amp;amp;amp;quot;
             augroup END
             endif
         endif
    endif
endif
